results.content:
Meanwhile, the technical reality of agentic shopping remains far from seamless. Maher, who has personally tested various agentic solutions, puts his current success rate at only around 70 percent. His experiences include agents purchasing items that were out of stock, failing to select appropriate shipping methods, and causing multi-week delays in delivery.

For a consumer, these are frustrating glitches, and for a retailer, they are the harbingers of a broken relationship. Maher warned that the "customer is always right" adage is being tested by this tsunami of AI, as users will likely direct their blame at both the AI provider and the brand when errors occur. ## Misleading Terms and Unfair Account Closure
I had a very disappointing experience with Sequence. After making legitimate transactions and using the service as intended, my account was suddenly closed without proper explanation. To make matters worse, the cashback rewards I was promised were withheld, despite being assured earlier that they would be included in the final payment. Additionally, I never received the remaining balance from my account, despite multiple follow-ups. Their lack of transparency regarding the terms for forfeiting rewards and their poor communication has made this experience frustrating. Sequence needs to be clearer about their policies and ensure that customers are treated fairly, especially when they have acted in good faith. [...] August 20, 2024

## No response to data privacy questions 😳🧐
I reached out to Sequence weeks ago for clarification on their privacy policy, to their head of customer service vial LinkedIn, while he was friendly and promised help, understood why I was asking about privacy, ultimately no one at Sequence got back to me.  
  
—Though the CEO did check out my LinkedIn profile, suggesting that my question was flagged to the c-suite.  
  
Nobody responded about how (besides in service delivery) all one’s financial data is used or shared. I nudged the customer service lead again, he apologized for the delay, but still...nothing.   
  
For companies that value security, this is a concerning signal, that Sequence can’t clearly articulate their privacy policy.

results.title: Why most agentic AI projects fail and how to succeed | Gideon Mendels posted on the topic | LinkedIn
results.content: Agentic AI isn’t broken. The way most teams are building it is. MIT recently said 95% of agentic AI projects are failing. That sounds about right. Here’s why: ➡️ Getting an agent to “work sometimes” is easy ➡️ Getting it reliable enough for production is hard Most teams think success comes from picking the right LLM or framework. It doesn’t. In reality, almost all the leverage is in the \system prompts\: the orchestrator logic, the tools, the glue. The only way to improve them is by: • Collecting real examples of success and failure • Tuning and testing against them • Iterating through edge cases With Opik, I see two types of teams: Those who keep swapping models and frameworks Those who methodically build a golden dataset and test against it Only one group ends up in the 5% that succeed.
